boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Byram's Ford (Big Blue River) record (October 22-23, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. The frozen interval covers Shelby's forcing of the Big Blue on October 22 and Pleasonton's forcing of Byram's Ford on the 23rd. The October 22 fight with Kansas militia south of the ford near Hickman's Mills and the Westport battle (MO027) are recorded separately and not added. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads the 1st Division, Army of the Border and the provisional cavalry division against Shelby's and Marmaduke's divisions; the live field reads zero. Price says Curtis's arrival raised Blunt's army on the Big Blue to between 6,000 and 8,000. Britton says Jennison's First Brigade held Byram's Ford, reinforced by the Sixteenth Kansas and the Fourth Kansas State Militia, against Thompson's brigade, and that on the 23rd Philips's brigade, then Winslow's and Sanborn's, attacked Marmaduke's division.
claims.rationale: A Confederate estimate of the whole Union line and unit identifications; no count at the ford. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS calls Byram's Ford the best ford in the area. Britton says the Big Blue's banks were steep with few good fords for trains and artillery, the ford's approaches were obstructed by felled trees and breastworks, and on the 23rd a Confederate battery on the crest above the ford swept the road. Price calls the Federal position strong by nature and strengthened by fortifications.
claims.rationale: Ground and works described by a summary, a history and an interested report; no map verification. The obstructions were made by the defenders, but the phase is left unresolved.

claims.value: Britton says Blunt sent Jennison to the ford, Thompson dismounted part of his brigade to wade the river, and on the 23rd Pleasonton arrested Brown and put Philips in command of the First Brigade, which forced the ford. Price says Shelby crossed with the rest of his division. The frozen commanders are Brigadier Generals Joseph Shelby and John S. Marmaduke and Major Generals James G. Blunt and Alfred Pleasonton; the live page lists Blunt and Shelby, both as Brigadier General.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; no automatic sole credit, and live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. On the 22nd, Britton and NPS say Shelby forced Jennison back toward Westport; on the 23rd, NPS says Marmaduke fell back after three hours and Price says Marmaduke had to fall back when his ammunition was exhausted. The result field covers both days.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown and the live field zero. Britton gives the Fourth Missouri State Militia's loss on the morning of the 23rd as 2 officers and 7 men killed and 3 officers and 44 men wounded, and the Kansas militia's loss south of the ford on the 22nd as 36 killed, 43 wounded and 100 prisoners; the latter action is not added to this record.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Blunt's, Jennison's, Pleasonton's, Philips's, Kelly's and Lazear's reports, Shelby's, Thompson's and Clark's reports and a map of the Big Blue fords remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
